author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Flags on New Hampshire public buildings and grounds were lowered to half-staff Friday as the state observed 25 years since the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Gov. Kelly Ayotte issued the directive Thursday, setting the observance from sunrise until sunset on September 11. The order applied across state-owned public facilities and accompanied remembrance events organized by cities, towns, fire departments and veterans groups.

New Hampshire lost 42 people in the attacks, according to anniversary reporting by state broadcasters. Communities held ceremonies throughout the day, including memorial dedications in Dover and Meredith and traditional moments of silence tied to the times the hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center and Pentagon and crashed in Pennsylvania.

The flag order did not add new closures or service changes. Its purpose was ceremonial: creating a visible statewide marker while local communities remembered residents, first responders and military members connected to the attacks and their aftermath. Flags were scheduled to return to full staff after sunset Friday.
dek: Flags on state public buildings and grounds were directed to remain at half-staff from sunrise through sunset Friday.
headline: New Hampshire lowers public flags for September 11 anniversary
